raw_response:
I've been farming this same land in Quzhou for over forty years. My father grew wheat and corn here before me, and I'll do the same. There's no reason to change what works.

My land is about 12 mu. I can't manage more at my age, and my son is in the city. Some neighbors have switched to vegetables or rented their fields to cooperatives, but I don't trust that. I know wheat and corn. I know this soil.

For wheat, I'll plough deep in October before sowing — I always plough, rotary tilling doesn't turn the soil over properly for wheat. I'll buy Jimai 22 seed from the county supply store, same as last year. For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer before planting and add urea at jointing. I irrigate three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. Two pesticide sprays — one for aphids, one for rust if I see it.

After harvest in June I go straight into summer corn. I use a rotary tiller then because there's no time — corn needs to go in fast. I buy hybrid seed,郑单958 or whatever is available at the store. Corn gets more nitrogen than wheat, split into two applications. I irrigate at silking stage and once more if it's dry. Usually just one pesticide pass for army worm.

I don't do soil tests. I apply what I've always applied. My yields are stable, around 450 for wheat and 550 for corn. That's enough.
